opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of Erdős problem #856: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: Erdős asked how large the sum of reciprocals of a subset of the first N integers can be if no k of its elements share the same pairwise least common multiple. In July 2026 RayYoung, Keheng Zhu and Yanping Luo listed a claimed solution giving the exponent of log N exactly, as a finite extremal formula, in an Overleaf document. The authors say they checked the argument themselves and did not formalise it. There is no fixed file to pin and no Lean development. Everything here is open.

background.spoken: For k at least three, let f_k(N) be the largest possible sum of 1/n over a subset of the integers one to N that contains no k elements with the same pairwise least common multiple. Estimate f_k(N). Erdős gave an upper bound of order log N over log log N; Tang and Zhang in 2025 showed f_k(N) lies between two powers of log N with exponents strictly between zero and one, exponents tied to the sunflower conjecture.

background.term: The claim by RayYoung, Keheng Zhu and Yanping Luo
background.spoken: The claim is that f_k(N) equals (log N) to the power gamma_k plus o(1), where gamma_k is a supremum over finite block parameters of a quantity built from the largest r-uniform family on n points with no k sets sharing the same pairwise union. Matching weighted upper and lower bounds reduce the problem to that finite extremal formula. The authors say the proof is short, that they checked it themselves and uploaded it after minor revisions without a Lean formalisation, and that it builds on the existing literature and the problem's discussion thread.
